Sure! Here’s a simple yet flavorful way to make an **Indian‑style grilled steak** with a quick tandoori‑inspired rub and a creamy yogurt sauce. Feel free to adjust spice levels to your taste. --- ## Ingredients | Item | Quantity | |------|----------| | Ribeye or sirloin steak (1–1.5 lb) | 1 piece | | Plain Greek yogurt | ½ cup | | Lemon juice | 2 Tbsp | | Garlic paste | 1 Tbsp | | Ginger paste | 1 Tbsp | | Ground cumin | 1 tsp | | Ground coriander | 1 tsp | | Garam masala | ½ tsp | | Turmeric powder | ¼ tsp | | Paprika (smoked or sweet) | 1 tsp | | Kashmiri red chili powder (or paprika + cayenne) | 1 tsp (adjust for heat) | | Salt | ½ tsp | | Black pepper | ¼ tsp | | Olive oil or melted butter | 1 Tbsp | | Fresh cilantro, chopped | 2 Tbsp (for garnish) | | Optional: sliced onions & bell peppers | for grilling alongside | ### For the Yogurt Sauce (optional but recommended) | Item | Quantity | |------|----------| | Plain Greek yogurt | ¾ cup | | Minced garlic | 1 clove | | Lemon juice | 1 Tbsp | | Fresh mint leaves, chopped | 1 Tbsp | | Fresh cilantro, chopped | 1 Tbsp | | Salt | ¼ tsp | | Water or milk | to thin (if needed) | --- ## Instructions ### 1. Prepare the Marinade 1. In a bowl, whisk together: - ½ cup yogurt - 2 Tbsp lemon juice - 1 Tbsp each of garlic & ginger paste - 1 tsp cumin, coriander, garam masala, turmeric, paprika, and Kashmiri chili powder - ½ tsp salt & ¼ tsp black pepper - 1 Tbsp olive oil or melted butter 2. Mix until smooth; you’ll get a thick, creamy mixture. ### 2. Marinate the Steak 1. Pat the steak dry with paper towels. 2. Rub the yogurt mixture all over the steak, ensuring it’s coated evenly. 3. Cover and refrigerate for at least **30 minutes** (up to 4 hours). If you’re short on time, even 15 minutes will add flavor. ### 3. Preheat Your Grill or Skillet - **Grill:** Heat to high (medium‑high if using a gas grill). - **Skillet:** Use a cast‑iron or heavy skillet; preheat over medium‑high heat. ### 4. Cook the Steak | Step | Details | |------|---------| | **Sear** | Place steak on the grill/skillet. Sear 2–3 min per side for a nice crust. | | **Finish** | Reduce heat to medium. Continue cooking to your preferred doneness:
• Rare: 120–125 °F (48–52 °C)
• Medium‑rare: 130–135 °F (54–57 °C)
• Medium: 140–145 °F (60–63 °C)
Use a meat thermometer for accuracy. | | **Rest** | Remove steak, tent loosely with foil, and let rest 5–7 min. This allows juices to redistribute. | *Optional:* While the steak rests, you can grill sliced onions & bell peppers for a smoky side. ### 5. Make the Yogurt Sauce (If Desired) 1. Combine ¾ cup yogurt, minced garlic, 1 Tbsp lemon juice, chopped mint & cilantro, and ¼ tsp salt in a small bowl. 2. Whisk until smooth. Add water/milk a tablespoon at a time to reach desired consistency. 3. Chill briefly before serving. ### 6. Plate & Serve 1. Slice the rested steak against the grain into ⅜–½ inch thick slices. 2. Drizzle or spoon the yogurt sauce over the slices. 3. Garnish with fresh cilantro. 4. Pair with naan, basmati rice, or a simple cucumber raita for a complete meal. --- ## Tips & Variations - **Heat Level:** Adjust Kashmiri chili or add a pinch of cayenne for extra heat. - **Flavor Boost:** Add a splash of soy sauce or Worcestershire sauce to the yogurt mix for umami depth. - **Vegetarian Alternative:** Swap steak for thick-cut paneer or tofu; marinate similarly and grill for 3–4 min per side. - **Leftovers:** Store leftover steak in the fridge; reheat gently in a pan with a splash of water or broth to keep it moist. Enjoy your homemade Indian‑style steak—rich, aromatic, and surprisingly easy to pull off!
